question_text: LAN stands for and refers to:
option_a: Local Area Network -- a network set up in one building
option_b: Long Area Network -- a network spanning countries
option_c: Linked Application Node -- a type of software
option_d: Live Access Network -- a wireless-only network
explanation: LAN stands for Local Area Network and refers to a network set up in one building.

question_text: MAN stands for Metropolitan Area Network and refers to:
option_b: Two LANs linked between two buildings in the same metropolis
option_d: A network used only by government
explanation: MAN is a Metropolitan Area Network and refers to two LANs linked between two buildings in the same metropolis.

question_text: This unit describes three typical network topologies (layouts). Which of the following is one of them?
explanation: The three typical network topologies are star, ring, and bus shapes.

question_text: In a star network topology, how do outlying stations communicate?
option_a: Directly with each other with no central device
explanation: In the star shape (the most common topology), outlying stations communicate through a central hub device.

question_text: Which device converts electronic signals into sound pulses suitable for transmission over telephone lines, enabling WAN connections?
explanation: A Modem (Modulator-Demodulator) converts electronic signals into pulses of sound that can be sent along telephone lines.
URL stands for Universal (Uniform) Resource Locator, simply another word for a web address.

question_text: According to this unit, who controls access to the web, requiring users to sign on before getting internet access?
explanation: An Internet Service Provider (ISP) controls access to the web; a person has to sign on with an ISP before getting onto the Internet, normally for a monthly fee.

question_text: Which term describes multimedia files (text, graphics, sound, video) that are attached to an email?
explanation: Attachments are multimedia files 'attached' to an email; they can be text, graphics, sound, video, spreadsheet, database, or an entire application.

question_text: Which term describes software that gives a graphical interactive interface for searching, finding, viewing, and managing information over a network?
explanation: A browser is application software that gives a graphical interactive interface for searching, finding, viewing, and managing information over a network.

question_text: According to this unit, what is a Newsgroup best described as?
option_b: An electronic bulletin board where messages are left for others to see and respond to
explanation: A Newsgroup is basically an electronic bulletin board where messages are left for others to see and respond to, enabling two-way communication.

question_text: The area on the Internet that comprises thousands of newsgroups is known as:
explanation: The area on the Internet that comprises thousands of newsgroups is known as the Usenet.

question_text: Newsgroup messages are stored on Internet servers called:
explanation: Newsgroup messages are stored on Internet servers called News Servers, located throughout the world; each ISP supplies one for its subscribers.

question_text: According to this unit, does the recipient of an email need to be actively connected to the network at the moment a message is sent?
option_b: No -- the message is stored in the email database until the recipient connects
option_d: Email cannot be sent unless both parties are online
explanation: If a person is not attached to the network when a message is sent, the message is stored in the email database until they attach to the network.

question_text: In the New Message window described in this unit, which box is used to give a message a subject heading?
explanation: The Subject: box is for giving the message a subject heading, which is also used as the message title in the title bar.

question_text: In the New Message window, which box is used if you want to send the same message to another person, in addition to the primary recipient?
explanation: The Cc... box is used if you want to send the same message to another person, in addition to the primary recipient in the To... box.

question_text: In a ring network topology, how are computers connected to one another?
option_b: In a closed loop, with each computer connected to two others
explanation: In a ring topology, computers are connected in a closed loop, with each computer connected to two neighbouring computers, forming a ring.

question_text: WAN stands for Wide Area Network and is best described as:
option_a: A network confined to a single room
option_b: A network that spans a large geographic area, potentially across countries
option_c: A network with no computers at all
explanation: A Wide Area Network (WAN) spans a large geographic area, potentially connecting computers across cities or countries.

question_text: According to this unit, what does 'http' at the beginning of a web address stand for?
explanation: HTTP stands for Hyper Text Transfer Protocol, the protocol used for transferring web pages over the internet.

question_text: According to this unit, can anyone read and respond to messages posted in a public newsgroup?
option_a: No, only the original poster can see it
option_b: Yes -- newsgroups enable two-way communication where anyone can read and respond
option_d: Newsgroups do not allow responses at all
explanation: Newsgroups enable two-way communication -- anyone accessing the newsgroup can read a posted message and respond to it.
